title: Uniform truncation bound for derived direct image
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with $S$ quasi-compact, and let $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ be the category of complexes with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-pc-derived-category]. Then there is a positive integer $N$ such that every $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ with $H^m(E)=0$ for all $m>0$ satisfies $H^m(Rf_*E)=0$ for every $m\ge N$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image]. Consequently, for every $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ and every integer $q$, the natural map $H^q(Rf_*E)\to H^q(Rf_*\tau_{\ge -n}E)$ induced by $E\to\tau_{\ge -n}E$ [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] is an isomorphism for all sufficiently large integers $n$.

proof.text: Choose N>0 from the uniform nonpositive derived-image bound. Retain this bound as the first conjunct.

For fixed E,q choose n0=N-q. If n>=n0, then N<=q+n+1 and N<=(q+1)+n+1. Apply the shifted truncation tail bound in degrees q and q+1. Apply the triangulated derived direct-image functor to the standard truncation triangle. The proved upstream lemma DerivedCategory.isIso_homologyMap_mor₂, which packages the Mathlib long exact homology sequence and the mono/epi criterion in an abelian category, makes the second arrow an isomorphism from these two vanishings. The second arrow is exactly the canonical lower-truncation map under higher direct image.
